Earlier Counterpoint Research reports already showed Apple recording its strongest-ever second-quarter iPhone shipment performance, and Omdia has also released its own data today, pointing to the same record-breaking results. Details below.

Omdia warns: even steeper declines are yet to come

Earlier today, we reported on a Counterpoint Research report that listed preliminary data on global smartphone shipments for the second quarter of 2026.

Counterpoint's report noted that Samsung led the market with a 24% shipment share, up from 20% a year earlier; Apple followed closely at 20%, up from 17% the previous year. Xiaomi fell from 14% to 12%, OPPO from 12% to 11%, and vivo from 9% to 8%.

Now Omdia's preliminary report (via MacMagazine) shows the same broad trend, though with slightly different specific estimates.

Omdia estimated Samsung at 22%, up from 20% in the second quarter of 2025; Apple came in second at 20%, up from 16% the previous year. Xiaomi fell from 15% to 11%, OPPO from 12% to 10%, and vivo from 9% to 8%.

Below are Omdia's comments on Apple's performance this quarter:

Omdia noted that, unsurprisingly, the ongoing memory chip shortage caused overall shipments to fall 4% year-over-year, making the second quarter of 2026 the weakest quarter for the market since the second quarter of 2023.
